newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus Vassiliko 96 turnover, profits up.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus Vassiliko 96 turnover, profits up.

text.p: Cypriot cement manufacturer Vassiliko on Thursday said 1996 was the best year in the history of the company, bolstered by higher sales locally and a surge in exports.
The company, which is 33 percent owned by the Italcementi group, posted pre-tax profits of 5.55 million pounds ($10.7 million) in 1996, a 9.8 percent rise from a year earlier.
Turnover in 1996 reached 26.3 million, compared to 24.5 million in 1995. The board plans to propose a dividend of 4.5 cents per share compared with 3.0 cents issued in 1995.
The company, formed in 1963, exports cement mainly to countries in the Middle East region.
Chairman Panos Ghalanos, speaking ahead of the annual meeting of the company on Friday, said prospects for 1997 were equally good.
He said an estimated 10 percent slowdown in demand on the local market in the first six months of 1997 has not had an impact on sales.
"Total sales of cement and clinker have not been affected in the first six months because of the good performance of our exports," he told a news conference.
Its main markets are Israel and Lebanon.
Vassiliko is one of two local cement companies and the only exporter of cement. Its own harbour on the southern coast of the island, next to its production plant, allows it to export all year round.
Cement sales on the local market rose by 5.1 percent in 1996, giving Vassiliko an estimated 63 percent share of the local market, Ghalanos said.
Sales reached 1,168.000 tonnes in 1996 versus 1,136.000 tonnes in 1995. The company exports more than 500,000 tonnes of cement annually.
Italcementi initially acquired a 20 percent stake in the company in 1990, then increased it to 33 percent in January of this year.

The cooperation has had good results for the Cypriot firm, Ghalanos said. "With the technical know how of our Italian associates the factory succeeded in significantly upgrading the production capacity of its existing units," he said.
